correctness.rationale: The fixed-chain dual equivalence is Theorem 4.4 of arXiv:2212.14756, with the required (S1)-(S3) in Definition 4.1. On the n-point dual chain, requiring both sets of empty and nonempty row (and column) indices to be upsets eliminates mixed emptiness. For nonempty row intervals [a_i,b_i], preserving all upsets under g and f makes both endpoints nonincreasing. Coverage of every column is equivalent to a_last=0, b_first=n-1 and b_next>=a_prev-1. Conversely those conditions imply all row and column fibers are nonempty intervals with nonincreasing endpoints, hence all four operations preserve upsets. The duality is faithful and g(U_t) is exactly {i:a_i<t}. Therefore g profiles are unique, every nonincreasing a ending at zero is realized, and all b completions are counted with no collisions. Stars-and-bars gives 1+binomial(2n-2,n-1) reducts and maximum fiber binomial(2n-2,n-1); two explicit b vectors give the minimum two for n>=2, attained for a=(n-1,...,n-1,0). Independent exhaustive tests evaluate the original algebraic T1-T8 on chains of size 2..4, all admissible relations through 4 dual points, and endpoint formulas through 5 dual points. The arbitrary-n proof is deductive, not inferred from the finite tests.

value.rationale: Exact inverse fibers of the four-to-one negative tense reduct are an intrinsic reconstruction invariant: they quantify which single modalities extend and how many complete operator structures they admit. The sharp general nonfaithfulness theorem for every nonzero reduct on chains of at least three elements, the extremal fibers, and the complete parameter classification solve the natural representation/reconstruction question raised by the established negative-tense duality. This is a complete finite-family classification rather than a merely computed initial sequence; the proof explains and controls all n, with clear application to information loss between unary and four-operator semantics.
